content.title: Randomized Trials Comparing Endarterectomy With Stenting in Symptomatic Patients With Carotid Stenosis

trials.key_features: Single center; patients with symptomatic carotid stenosis >70%.
trials.comments: Terminated prematurely because of safety concerns.

trials.key_features: Multicenter; patients of any age with symptomatic or asymptomatic carotid stenosis suitable for CEA or CAS.
trials.p_value: NS in original article; OR not reported
trials.comments: Follow-up to 3 y; relatively low stent use (26%) in CAS group.

trials.key_features: Single center; patients with symptomatic carotid stenosis >70% (events within 3 mo of evaluation).
Multicenter randomized trial of patients with ≥80% asymptomatic carotid stenosis (70%) and ≥50% symptomatic carotid stenosis (30%).
trials.comments: Terminated prematurely because of a drop in randomization.

trials.key_features: Multicenter; patients with symptomatic carotid stenosis >60% within 120 d before enrollment suitable for CEA or CAS.
trials.comments: Study terminated prematurely because of safety and futility issues; concerns about operator inexperience in the CAS arm and nonuniform use of embolism protection devices.

trials.key_features: Multicenter; patients >50 y old with symptomatic carotid stenosis >70% in the 180 d before enrollment.
trials.primary_endpoint: Ipsilateral ischemic stroke or death from time of randomization to 300 d after the procedure
trials.comments: Study terminated prematurely after futility analysis; concerns about operator inexperience in the CAS arm and nonuniform use of embolism protection devices.

trials.key_features: Multicenter, randomized, open, assessor-blinded, noninferiority trial. Compared outcome after CAS with outcome after CEA in 527 patients who had carotid stenosis of at least 60% that had recently become symptomatic.
trials.major_outcome_events: Up to 4 y for any periprocedural stroke or death

hazard_ratio.p: 0.04 for any stroke or periprocedural death; 0.08 for any stroke or death; 0.03 for CAS vs CEA

trials.comments: A hazard function analysis showed 4y differences in cumulative probabilities of outcomes between CAS and CEA were largely accounted for by the higher periprocedural (within 30 d of the procedure) risk of stenting compared with endarterectomy. After the periprocedural period, the risk of ipsilateral stroke was low and similar in the 2 treatment groups.
